pages.x: Ranked by points for what made it into the guide.
Find your Chief’s Office band; each card says what to build, train and research next.
THE ONE RULE: Keep the Academies training and research running, and shield up before you log off.
THE ONE RULE: Check any figure on a page marked Not updated or verified in your own game before you spend on it.

THE ONE RULE: Finish a Chief’s Office level, raise Dispatch Center and the named second building to match, then start the next level. Every Chief’s Office level has a padlock: it needs Dispatch Center and one other building at a set level first. Each new level then opens troop tiers, events and buildings. The table below lists both for every level from 2 to 45.
THE ONE RULE: Plan every push from your real timer: base time divided by 1 plus your construction-speed bonus.

THE ONE RULE: Always train the highest tier you have, in all three Academies at once. Officers are your troops. There are three classes: Guards stand in front and take the hits, Marksmen deal the damage from behind, and Bikers sit between and counter Marksmen. Each class trains in its own Academy.Tiers run from T1 to T10. Your Academy level sets the highest tier you can train, and an Academy can’t go past your Chief’s Office level.

THE ONE RULE: Research Squad Queue I, II and III the moment each unlocks. Development is the Research Center tab that makes you faster: construction, research, training and healing speed, training and hospital capacity, and extra marches (Squad Queue).Tiers I to III of every line are cheap: none takes more than 8 hours. From tier IV the times jump to days, and that is where the order matters.

THE ONE RULE: Send three heroes, one per class, and fill every march to capacity with your highest tier. A march is what you send out on the map: one Guard hero, one Biker hero, one Marksman hero and as many officers as your deployment capacity allows. The game enforces one hero per class.All three heroes’ deploy skills and class lines count for the officers in their march. Hero order does not matter in your own march; it only matters when you join a rally.

Chief Almighty is a six-day event (Events button, right edge of the screen) where each day scores one kind of spending: building power one day, fragments another, training another, and so on. Points unlock chests (tiers) and a daily rank. The whole trick is to save each material and use it on its day.Each day runs 24 hours from 00:00 UTC. Points land when an action completes (a timer ends, a batch finishes, you press star-up), so a speedup only scores by finishing a timer on a day that pays for it. Tap a later day in Events → Chief Almighty to see its tasks before it starts. Use universal spee

THE ONE RULE: Spend Electro Cores on your main academy to Electro Level 3 first, and never start an upgrade you might cancel. Cancelling an Electro upgrade in progress refunds only 50% of the Electro Cores. Standard resources refund fully; speedups do not refund at all. Electro Core is a top-rarity currency that unlocks when your Chief’s Office reaches Level 30. It takes seven key buildings past building level 30 into Electro Levels, 0 to 3. The payoff is capacity buffs, a stronger Officer squad and, at Electro Level 3, a new combat skill for each academy. Every step also costs large amounts o

THE ONE RULE: Six heroes get materials; everyone else lives on event drops. Fragments are the pieces of a hero. Enough of them recruit it, more raise its stars. A hero’s own fragments work on that hero only; universal fragments work on heroes of that rarity you already own. You get them from recruitment, events and shops.Skill books level skills. Patrol books level the Arena skills (left column on the Skills tab); Deployment books level the march skills (right column). The book’s rarity must match the hero’s.

THE ONE RULE: Push stars to the next skill gate (sub-star 6, 12, 18 or 24), then stop until you have the books to use it. Every hero has five stars of six sub-stars each, 30 steps in all. Fragments buy sub-stars. Stars raise the hero’s class line (Attack and Defense of that class of troops in the march) and decide how high each skill can go.Skill levels cost books; hero levels cost hero experience. Levels raise the hero’s own card, which matters in the Arena, but never the class line.

THE ONE RULE: Keep Scarlett, Andre and Brooke fed; treat Generation 1 Epics as temporary. Heroes arrive in generations. Generation 1 is the launch roster. Generation 2 adds three Epics (Sea-ah, Hikari, Dmitry) and three Legendaries (Samuel, Pamela, Franklin). Generation 3 adds Marcus, Duke and Lexie.Your state’s age decides when they come, not your level. The state day counter is under Events. Each new Legendary generation grows faster (1.20, then 1.50), so don’t sink fragments into a hero a later one replaces.
THE ONE RULE: Put Scarlett in the Biker slot of your main march and give her Legendary deploy books before anyone else.
THE ONE RULE: Run Brooke in the Guard slot until Andre passes Star 3, then make her the Guard of your garrison.
THE ONE RULE: Keep levelling Tony after Lucy takes his slot: Streamlined Logistics cuts every building’s cost and time just by owning him.
THE ONE RULE: Give Andre every one of his own fragments: his class line climbs 1.30 times as fast as any other Legendary’s.
THE ONE RULE: Pour every Epic universal fragment into Lucy until Star 4, then she takes the Marksman slot from Tony.
THE ONE RULE: Level Leon’s deploy skills right after Lucy’s: he is your third-march Guard (main Guard without Brooke or Andre) and the Arena swap when a lineup dies too fast.
THE ONE RULE: Use Vixen as the Biker of your second march, and spend nothing on her while Scarlett still needs it.
THE ONE RULE: Give Gary Epic deploy books only once Lucy, Leon and Vixen have theirs at level 5.
THE ONE RULE: Spend Sea-ah’s first 10 fragments on Star 1: that switches on Blueprint Simulation, research speed that works while she sits at home.
THE ONE RULE: Take Hikari to Star 1 (10 fragments) and leave her at home: Caring Heart speeds up your Hospital from the bench.
THE ONE RULE: Send Dmitry in the march when you chase criminals: Born for the Chase counts only while he is in that march.
THE ONE RULE: Keep Rix on the bench: neither of his deploy skills helps in a fight.

THE ONE RULE: Spend nothing on Rares except Rare deploy books into Gus’s and Zoc’s production skills. Zoc, Gus, Cassie and Alvin each boost one resource: a production skill for the building that makes it, and a confiscation skill for gathering it on the map. Their ratio is 0.65, so they never fight well.Boot Camp keeps their level up for free. The only thing worth buying for them is the production skill, and only for the resource you run short of.

THE ONE RULE: Promote old stacks when a new tier opens; never train low tiers planning to promote them later. Promotion turns officers you already own into your highest unlocked tier (Academy → Promote tab). You keep the count and pay only the difference between the old tier’s cost and the new one’s.Training adds new officers. Promotion makes the ones you have stronger. Which one you need depends on whether your marches are already full.

THE ONE RULE: Level all six pieces together, and do your upgrading on Chief Almighty day 6. Hold Reinforced Metal, Tactical Gel and Classified Schematics for Chief Almighty day 6. Day 6 scores every point of equipment rating you add; the same upgrade on another day scores nothing there. Chief equipment is six pieces you wear, not a hero: two for Guards, two for Bikers, two for Marksmen. Every level on a piece adds Attack and Defense for that class, for every officer in every march.Each piece climbs the same 26 levels. Levels cost Reinforced Metal, Tactical Gel and, from level 5, Classified Sch

THE ONE RULE: Save every Badge Blank and Warrant, then take all 18 badges to level 3 before any goes to level 4. Badges add the two stats chief equipment does not: Health and Penetration. Each of your six chief equipment pieces holds three badges, one per class, so you have 18 badges and six per class.Badge Blanks and Warrants drop long before badges open, and nothing else uses them. Keep every one.

THE ONE RULE: Keep your Legendary pieces level with each other, and forge only on Chief Almighty day 5. Hold Hardened Steel for Chief Almighty day 5. Every bar of steel you forge with that day scores; forging on another day throws those points away. Hero gear is four pieces a hero wears: helmet, gloves, armor and boots. A piece belongs to a class, not a hero, so a Guard piece fits whichever Guard hero you run, one hero at a time.Two pieces carry the class Health line and two the class Penetration line. That class line is the march buff. You raise it with Enhance (Bulletproof Fibers) and, on Le

THE ONE RULE: Take Gemini to +5 first, and use weapon materials only on Chief Almighty day 5. Spend exclusive weapon materials on Chief Almighty day 5. They score more per item that day than anything else in the event; used on another day they score nothing there. Every Legendary hero has an exclusive weapon: a fifth equipment slot only that hero can use. It unlocks at Star 1 and cannot be unequipped.Each weapon level adds Health and Penetration for the hero’s whole class, flat stats on the hero’s card, and steps up one of two weapon skills. It is raised with that hero’s own weapon material.

THE ONE RULE: Do not Empower a piece to +1 until you have settled which hero and slot it is for: it can never be reforged afterwards. Mythic is not a new rarity. It is a Legendary hero gear piece pushed past enhancement level 100, up to 200, with a separate Empower button. Empower costs Legendary pieces and Valor Crystals instead of experience, at six milestone levels.The point of it is the Deploy talents: four pieces at +100 give +200% Attack and +200% Defense to one troop class on the map.

THE ONE RULE: Finish every tier III before you start any tier IV, cheapest per hour first. Battle research makes your officers stronger: Attack, Defense, Penetration and Health for each class, four Squad lines that help all three classes, and Troop Expansion for bigger marches.Every class line has six tiers. Tier III always adds +11.5 points and tier IV +22.5, but the hours differ a lot between lines. Research time decides the order.

THE ONE RULE: Donate to the recommended line every day. Alliance tech is research the whole alliance shares. Members donate resources to a line, and every member gets the buff once it is researched.R4 and R5 choose which line is “recommended” (the green thumb). Members only need to donate there; the order below is for the officers who pick the recommendation.

THE ONE RULE: Keep the Chief’s Office upgrading; between its levels, build only what its padlock names. Your city has 23 buildings: 18 that level up and five fixed ones (Hero Hall, Arena, Intel Center, Monument, Recovery Center). The Chief’s Office is the gate. Every other building, troop tier and event checks its level.Every upgrade has a padlock that lists what must be built first: usually the Chief’s Office at that level plus one or two other buildings. Tap the next Chief’s Office level and its padlock is your to-do list.

pages.t: What to buy at each budget
pages.x: THE ONE RULE: Set a monthly budget, buy down the ladder from the top, and never buy because of a countdown. An offer is anything sold for real money: diamond top-ups, packs (a fixed bundle at a fixed price), passes (a reward track that pays over days), the Growth Fund (pays at each Chief’s Office level) and the pop-ups after upgrades. They live under the Store (bottom bar) and the Events button.The “value %” badge prices every item at the raw top-up rate, speedups and resources included. That is how a badge reaches 3,000%. Score packs yourself, with items you would not buy counted as zero. Not

THE ONE RULE: Put every scrap of Tactical Gel into chief equipment and spend speedups only on scoring days. Free-to-play: no money spent. Everything comes from events, event shops and daily freebies. A free account can build a competitive march. It can’t get Brooke, and chief-equipment materials come slowly.

THE ONE RULE: Spend diamonds only on what time can’t buy: fragments, Tactical Gel, Hardened Steel and skill books. Diamonds are the premium currency, earned from events, ranks, achievements and packs. They buy almost anything, so spend them only on what you can’t otherwise get. Speedups bought with diamonds leave nothing behind. Prices are on Shops and prices.

THE ONE RULE: In every shop buy the materials it is short of, and skip the speedups and resources it pads the list with. Each shop takes its own currency: diamonds, Hero Tokens, Arena coins, alliance points, Assessment Coins or event badges. What each item is worth buying is on Where to spend diamonds.

THE ONE RULE: Reach VIP 6 from daily log-ins and the alliance store; never buy VIP points with diamonds. VIP is a level you raise with VIP points. Points come from daily log-ins, the alliance store, VIP point packs and purchases. Each level adds a perk, and the VIP store and Honor packs open with it.

THE ONE RULE: When you join, put Andre (or Vixen) in slot 1: only that hero’s first deploy skill counts. A rally is a group attack. One member opens it on a target with a countdown; others tap Join and send a march; it launches when the timer ends. Alliance → War lists the same rallies.The rally leader’s three heroes count in full. Each joiner adds its officers and the first deploy skill of its slot 1 hero, nothing else.

THE ONE RULE: Keep the Hospital bigger than the losses you expect, and leave a Guard-heavy defence at home. Your garrison defends your city when someone attacks it: the heroes at home plus the officers at home. Reinforcing means sending a march to sit in an ally’s garrison.Wounded defenders go to the Hospital. Wounded past Hospital capacity go to the Recovery Center; nobody dies until that is full too.

THE ONE RULE: Shield before you log off, and don’t leave a march garrisoned in a map structure when you need that shield. Anyone on the map can scout and attack your city while it has no shield. A Tactical Shield, used from the Backpack or bought in the Store, blocks attacks, scouts and rallies against you until it runs out or you break it.Start shielding around Chief’s Office 10. That is when losses start to hurt.

pages.t: Where to put your police station
pages.x: THE ONE RULE: Inside the border, next to an anchor, weakest innermost. Alliances keep their police stations together in a hive inside their territory: the area around the Alliance Headquarters and its flags. Help arrives by marching, so the closer you live, the sooner it lands.You move your police station with a teleport item from the Backpack.

THE ONE RULE: Scout first, then bring the class that beats what you see. To attack, tap a city on the map and Scout it first; the report lands in Mail. Then Attack with a march, or open a Rally for a group hit.Attacking breaks your own shield and locks it for 30 minutes (Defending your city). Your wounded go to your Hospital.

THE ONE RULE: Run Scarlett, Brooke, Tony, Andre and Lucy, all at the level cap. The Arena is the VS ring near the helipad in your city. Your five heroes fight another chief’s five, with no officers. Patrol stages are the same five-hero fight against the game.What fights is each hero’s Patrol block: the hero’s own Attack, Defense and Health (gear and weapon included), the Backups that ride with them, and their Patrol skills. Deploy skills do nothing here.

THE ONE RULE: Scout, two rallies a few minutes apart, then everyone shields together. As a member your job is short: be online, keep your shield until the caller says drop it, join the rally with the hero the leader asks for in slot 1, and send full marches.Leaders pick the target and the order of hits.

THE ONE RULE: Reinforce the two or three anchors; everyone else shields. As a member: keep a shield up when you are offline, reinforce the city the leaders call with Leon in slot 1, and keep your Hospital half empty before a war.Leaders pick the anchors and call the reinforcements.

THE ONE RULE: Your place in the alliance power list sets your job; hospital and heroes can move you. Alliances fight every war with the same five jobs: leaders who open rallies, anchors who get reinforced, a strike core that joins every rally, support that reinforces and rotates, and a home guard that shields and registers.Leaders sort Alliance → Members by power and adjust the bands once, in a mail, before the week’s first event.

THE ONE RULE: Name a holder for every structure before the fight: structures score, kills do not. Wounded in your Hospital, a march out or a burning wall and you cannot enter. Heal, recall and check your wall before the fight, or your team plays the hour one short. A one-hour battle of your alliance against one other alliance on its own 240 by 240 map. Eleven structures and the Resupply Spots score: the first capture pays a bonus, then the structure pays every minute you hold it. Killing enemy squads earns the alliance nothing.It is for the top 20 alliances by power. Nobody dies: wounded Offic

THE ONE RULE: Register every week; the lanes R4 and R5 set before each preparation phase ends decide the round, because nobody marches. Fewer than 10 registered and the whole alliance fails to match. Nobody plays. A member who leaves the alliance after matching still fights but loses every reward. A weekly tournament of your alliance against five others of similar tier, one round each. Every round is three lane fights at once, Left, Middle and Right. The side with squads left in a lane takes its flag; two flags win the round.Fights run by themselves and you watch the replay. Squads are never k

THE ONE RULE: Hold the Capitol for 3 unbroken hours: rotate fresh squads onto it, never charge in alone. No Tactical Shield inside the Forbidden Zone, and none while your march sits in the Capitol or a Cannon. Go in only with the war party; everyone who sends a march stays online with an empty Hospital. Every two weeks the whole server fights for the State Capitol and the four Cannons around it, over a 6-hour Occupation Phase. The first alliance to hold the Capitol for 3 unbroken hours wins at once; otherwise the longest total hold at 6 hours wins. The winning alliance then installs a Governor

THE ONE RULE: From season 3 register the Supermax first, and keep fresh squads inside until the 30-minute hold locks. R4 or R5 must hand out the Unifier and special pools within 24 hours, or they are gone. Only members still in the alliance can receive them. Name a distributor and a backup before the battle. Sixteen prisons sit on the state map: 4 Supermax Prisons around the State Capitol and 12 Prisons around the edge, each held by a Mafia garrison. Every round your alliance registers, breaks a garrison, and tries to hold the prison for 30 unbroken minutes. A season is 8 rounds; each new seas

THE ONE RULE: Points only decide which state attacks; 3 unbroken hours on the Capitol win the war. PvP scores only between chiefs within 3 Chief’s Office levels. Outside that window a battle that wounds 30,000 Officers pays zero to both sides. Check the level before you march. Your state against another state. For five and a half days both race for points in five prep stages; the state with more State Points wins prep and becomes the attacker. Then a 12-hour Capital War is fought on the losing state’s map. Holding its Capitol for 3 unbroken hours wins; otherwise the longest total hold at 12 ho

THE ONE RULE: Check your state day under Events and plan your diamonds and materials around what opens next. Events run on two clocks. The state day counts the days since your server opened and unlocks things once: Mythic empowerment, K9, Generation 3 heroes. The event calendar repeats: some events come round every week, others every two weeks or every 28 days.Both clocks turn over at 00:00 UTC. The calendar under Events shows the next date of every event before it opens.

THE ONE RULE: Line each milestone event up with its Chief Almighty day. Five milestone events rotate through the week: Police Department Development, Hero Program, Officer Program, Arms Race and Armed to the Teeth. Each is a solo event with four milestone chests along a progress bar plus a top-100 leaderboard. The task list under the bar says exactly what scores today.The events hub’s ongoing tab lists everything live with its timer; the calendar tab shows the week.

THE ONE RULE: Pick a difficulty you can fully clear in all 50 stages, and bank Energy before the event starts. Finish all 50 stages or forfeit the clear gift and the next difficulty. Stalling at stage 20 of a harder tier pays only partial rewards and unlocks nothing. Hot Pursuit is a 3-day event against the game with two halves. In the Solo half you pick one difficulty, scout a Fugitive onto the world map, march on it and climb a 50-stage ladder. Each Fugitive is a straight power check: if your march power beats it, you win. In the alliance half, Elite Bounty, once enough members have cleared

THE ONE RULE: Be online while an order runs: durations are in PD time, so “24 hours” is only 12 real minutes. “24 hours (PD time)” runs for 12 real minutes, but cooldowns are real hours. Every timed order except Rapid Construction runs in PD time; Rapid Construction runs in real time. Chief Orders are six one-shot city buffs you issue from the Press Office. Each costs Satisfaction, runs for a fixed time, then enters a cooldown. They cover an instant resource grant, faster building and multipliers on your crime-processing pipeline.Satisfaction comes only from interrogating suspects in the Inter

THE ONE RULE: Finish both free tasks, then buy Diamond cores only up to an exact pack cost: without paid packs, stop at 20 Dormant Cores. A two-day exchange event. You collect Dormant Cores (two capped tasks, a Diamond exchange, four paid packs) and trade them for Electro Packs holding Electro Cores, Electro Core Chests, resources and, from Uncommon up, VIP Points and an Alliance Gift for your whole alliance.Without paid packs the only pack you can afford is Common: 4 Dormant Cores each, 5 an event. Dormant Cores are their own item: they are not Storm & Subdue’s Depleted Cores. What Electro Co

THE ONE RULE: Hit the top two milestones of all seven Phases for 14 medals, spending stockpiled consumables on the Phase that scores them. Do not upgrade your Chief’s Office mid-event. Crossing a tier boundary can raise a Phase’s top target by 50–100% for the same reward. Medal ladder rungs are claimed by hand before the event closes. King of the Precinct is a 7-day competition across servers: Chiefs from many States pooled into one contest. Each day is its own Phase with a themed task list. Doing the listed actions earns Points; reaching a Phase’s point thresholds earns Medals of Honor, which

THE ONE RULE: Play the free tasks every day and top up once: 110 Marks needs both, and money alone stops at tier 3. Perfect free play reaches 102 Order Marks; the top tier costs 110. The 8-Mark gap can only be closed by a top-up, and three days of top-ups with no gameplay reach only 60 Marks. A three-day task board that pays Order Marks for world-map work (Criminals, Crime Boss rallies, Confiscation), hero recruitment or Power gain, and one purchase. Marks are cashed in at five milestone tiers: 10, 30, 50, 80 and 110. Tiers 1 to 4 are reachable for free. The task board wipes at 00:00 server ti

THE ONE RULE: Spend at least 600 Energy Drinks a day. Stages are paid once, retries are free; drinks decide how far you get. Never skip Normal stage 2-1 with Police Tape. A skipped 2-1 opens 2-2 but keeps every Advanced stage locked; only an actual win opens them. A 3-day shooting event with 80 Normal stages and 10 Advanced stages. Brooke stands in a fixed spot with 5 bullets. You hold to aim, slide to set direction and release to fire. Bullets ricochet. Kill every enemy before the ammo runs out. It needs Chief’s Office level 7 or higher.Energy Drinks, not aim, decide how far you get. You pay

THE ONE RULE: Spend every Depleted Core before the grace day ends, Electro Cores first. No new thugs spawn after day 2, and day 3 is spend-only. When the grace day ends, unspent Depleted Cores turn into one small Ammo bundle; a single core in the shop buys 1,000,000 Ammo. A two-day earn-and-spend event in the Intel Center. Each intel refresh adds two Magnetic Thugs to your list; each one you defeat pays 10 Depleted Cores. You spend the cores in the event’s exchange shop, whose best row is Electro Cores.A full shop costs 270 cores and two days of thugs pay about 120, so you choose what to buy.

THE ONE RULE: A chest opens only when every cell in its line is claimed, not just completed, so tap every cell. Finished is not claimed: a completed line leaves its chest dark until every cell in it is tapped. Do not spend 2,500 Diamonds unless you also buy the pack; without the grand chest the Diamonds do not come back. Bingo is a seven-day board of 15 tasks in a 5×3 grid. Each cell pays a small resource pack. Each of the 5 rows and 3 columns pays a chest, and all 15 cells pay a grand chest. The game re-skins it every few months: Energy Revolution, Donut Day, Party Gifts, Oktoberfest and the

THE ONE RULE: Open Legendary safes and refresh past the rest; a leftover surplus goes on the best Epic, never a Rare. Never refresh with an unopened Legendary safe on the board. A refresh discards every unopened safe, and the “don’t remind me today” box turns off the warning that stops you. A seven-day safe-cracking event in one window with three tabs. Daily tasks in Decipher Operations pay Vault Keys. Keys open safes in The Lost Vault. Safes drop Commendation Medals, which buy stock in the Reward Exchange. Safes also drop Decipher Chests, and a chest can return keys.Your free key supply is fi

THE ONE RULE: Spend every Cargo Manifest before the event ends; unspent or late-mailed Manifests are worthless. Auto-Inspect spends one Manifest every half second with no cap and no warning: untick auto-continue first. A three-day event where you spend Cargo Manifests to open containers on a 25-container freighter. One Manifest opens one container. 24 containers pay a common reward and the 25th holds the surprise gift you chose, so an inspection never returns nothing. Find the gift and the freighter clears: the board wipes, a new freighter sails in and your counter resets to zero.Manifests com

THE ONE RULE: Log in every 8 hours to redeploy your squads: nothing changes what a crate holds, so missions run are the whole event. Speedups here are Inspection Speedups only. Universal Speedups, including the ones from Storage Crates, do not work on missions, and there is no Diamond option. A five-day event, plus one claim day, where you send up to four Enforcement Squads on timed missions. Each squad comes back with a Storage Crate you open for its contents or merge into a higher crate. Nothing you do changes what a crate holds: it is rolled the moment the squad departs.Deploying costs noth

THE ONE RULE: Be online for the three Mobster waves and have Alliance HQ garrisoned before both Velvet Dons land. Two waves march on Alliance HQ, not your police station, and three only attack online chiefs. Nobody at HQ at +14:30 and +33:00 forfeits the two biggest waves; being offline at +8:00, +21:00 or +26:30 loses that wave for good. Mafia Attack is an alliance-wide defense event against the game, not other players. An R4 or R5 officer schedules a run; 20 waves of Mafia then march on every member’s police station and on the Alliance HQ over about 33 minutes. You defend your own police sta

THE ONE RULE: Join the next open rally, Andre or Vixen leading your first two joins; rostered captains start them on a 5:00 timer until last call. Joining any vault rally locks you out of both traps until 00:00 server time on the third calendar day. Stay in the alliance until the reward mail arrives or you forfeit the rewards. Join only your own alliance’s run. The Vault Trap is a coordinated 30-minute assault on a vault boss that does not hit back. Rostered captains start rallies on a staggered rotation; everyone else joins the next open rally. In a rally only the leader’s buffs apply to the

THE ONE RULE: Spend all nine attempts every day, rerolling free Exclusive tiles for a 200% badge and taking the smallest task you can clear. Unspent attempts are deleted at daily reset, and giving up an accepted task burns the attempt. Reroll the tile before you accept it; never accept and then dump. Alliance Mobilization is a six-day alliance-versus-alliance event on a two-week cycle, with a preview day before it opens and a settlement day after it closes. Members accept timed tasks from two boards. Each finished task pays Solo Points to you and adds to your alliance’s Alliance Points. Allian

THE ONE RULE: Be in your top-20 alliance when matchmaking starts, then run all your trucks every day: escorts and raids are 10,000 points each. Switch alliances after matchmaking and you lose all alliance points and ranking eligibility. You keep your chests. Matchmaking is the final hour before the event, and eligibility freezes then. Alliance Faceoff is a 6.5-day head-to-head point race between two top-20 alliances (top 20 by Power in your State). Nobody marches, rallies or fights. Each day the side whose members scored more total points wins that day and banks Victory Points. The overall win

THE ONE RULE: Recruit Rix with your first 10 fragments, then stop investing in him; keep rallying for the speedups and use all 50 rewarded joins a day. Wild West is a recurring 5-day event about one map boss, the Sunset Killer. Kill Criminals on the world map to get Spurs, spend a Spur to spawn a Sunset Killer near your PD, then win a rally against him. Wins pay Rix Fragments, speedups and resources.Rix is only sold here: his fragments drop from these rallies and he is not in the recruitment pool. Rallying is alliance-only: a Sunset Killer is visible only to the summoner’s alliance. You can st

THE ONE RULE: Only other players’ Officers score, defeated or injured. Criminals, the Vault and Faceoff pay nothing. 4,000 points and a top-1,000 finish, or no ranking reward. Stopping at the 1,000-point first tier forfeits the whole leaderboard payout. A 48-hour solo race where every point comes from defeating or injuring other players’ Officers: the Guard, Biker and Marksman troops from your academies.Your points climb four personal reward tiers, then rank you against your own server. There is no alliance score. The game even warns targets before it starts: the pre-start popup offers a Tacti

THE ONE RULE: Save your one Assist invite for an SSR truck, and raid SSR trucks first: one SSR raid pays as much as a whole N truck. Chief’s Office level 7 only previews the event; you need level 12 to play. Below level 12 your trucks show greyed out and every action (dispatch, raid, Assist Squad request) is blocked. A cross-server supply-run event. You dispatch trucks loaded with rewards. Each truck travels a random route for 3 to 4 hours, and on arrival you collect whatever is left on board. Any player outside your alliance, including players from other servers, can raid your trucks on the r

THE ONE RULE: Teleport into the center at 0:00, chase hidden fields at 10:00 and 20:00, and send one squad to the Refinery at 23:00 every battle. If a fight is incoming and you cannot win, recall. Recalling keeps all your collected oil. Losing drops a portion as pickups anyone can grab and puts your heroes into 5-minute recovery. A 30-minute free-for-all oil collection event. You capture oilfields, hunt patrols for tech experience, contest the Refinery and pick up scattered oil drops. Your Officers are free, unlimited and cannot die, so you can always deploy a full squad.It pays from three ind

THE ONE RULE: Sweep first, then push, and always stop on a stage that is a multiple of 10. Comprehensive Assessment on Sunday gets 5 failures for the whole week, and nothing restores a failed attempt. Wins are free; only losses cost an attempt, and there is no buyback. PD Assessment is a weekly rotation of six stage ladders. Each theme scores one system only (heroes, K9s, badges, tech or equipment) and switches off everything else. Your army, alliance buffs and consumables are worth nothing. It costs no troops: Officers are not injured, win or lose, and state deployment is untouched.Every stag

Drilling below the next breakpoint caps you at the lower tier and burns Whistles for nothing. K9s are always-on dogs from the K9 Tactical Center, a city building that opens on state day 55. Class line or squad skill: which counts more

A hero’s class line buffs only its own class of troops in the march. A squad-wide deploy skill (Attack, Penetration, chance-based damage, damage reduction) buffs every troop. Which one wins depends on how big your other buffs are. STAGE WHICH WINS EXAMPLE Early: research and chief gear small The bigger Legendary class line Tony over Lucy Later: those buffs past about 200% Squad-wide skills: a 1.5 skill multiplier beats a 60-point bigger line Lucy over Tony; Leon within 7% of Andre and Brooke The 200% crossover is our estimate from the measured class lines. March lineups: Marches › Lineup. Arena five: PvP › Arena.

The Nuclear Plant in the centre, the two Power Control Stations in the south corners, an Emergency Station at every corner, the Armory, Support Camp, Helicopter Base and Reactor between. The outer ring opens at 3:00, the centre at 15:00. RULE DETAIL Safe zones One per alliance, in opposite corners. Nobody can attack you there, and you can still attack and reinforce from it. Teleports 1 free teleport every 12 minutes (6 with the Helicopter Base), then Advanced Teleporters. Expect 5 to 10 in the hour; spend them on unlocks and emergencies, never in dead time. Free marches 5-minute cooldown, at most 10. Holding The holder’s march sits inside; teammates reinforce the same structure and it fights as one stack. One holder plus 2 to 4 reinforcers; 4 or 5 on the Nuclear Plant and each Power Control Station. Reinforce with your defence lineup (60 / 20 / 20, Leon in slot 1). Rotation The holder calls “hurt” in chat and the next reinforcer is already marching. An empty structure falls to the first enemy march. Your police station It sits on the battlefield and can be hit outside the safe zone. Its wall goes in seconds; at 0 you are sent to your safe zone and wait 12 minutes to re-enter. Covering your city Keep a defence lineup at home while you hold something, or sit in the safe zone: nothing can hit you there and you can still reinforce. Three beats six If a structure cannot be reinforced, give it up and stack the next one: three full garrisons beat six thin ones. A useful default: your weakest lane takes their strongest, your strongest takes their middle, your middle takes their weakest.

Hot Pursuit 3 days 50 stages, one difficulty solo + alliance boss 21-day cycle RULE DETAIL Window 3 days (72 hours), repeating every 21 days. Pick One difficulty per event. The highest you can choose is one above your best-ever cleared difficulty. Unlock The next difficulty needs all 50 stages of the current one cleared. Champion gates The Champion tab needs a server at least 179 days old. Champion Easy needs Hero Trial Hell cleared, all 50 stages. Pays A bundle on every kill, a best-stage mail, a difficulty-clear gift, and alliance boss rewards. Costs Energy: 25 a solo stage, 35 a rallied stage.

DO Finish the difficulty you can clear, then step up next event. Climb in order: solo until a stage beats you, then lead a rally on it, and only when the rally fails spend a Warrant to request assistance. Rally every wall: stages 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50. Budget 35 Energy for each. Bank donuts and never miss a Delicious Meal; use the 21 days between runs. Help allies daily. The first 5 helps refund a Warrant, and daily Rally rewards reset. Muster hitters first, then scout the boss, and schedule it at peak online hours. It lives 30 minutes. DON’T Overreach your difficulty. Hoard Warrants to scout with. Scouting costs Energy; a Warrant only opens your Fugitive to allies’ rallies, and unused ones are wiped. Burn Warrants early on stages you could solo or rally. You start with 5, and they are your last resort. Chase damage %. Boss rewards are flat per participant. Treat Champion as a reskin. It pays Safe resources, Lvl 2 chests and the 5K Hero EXP item, and never fewer than 15 Legendary fragments.

Only the next stage can be scouted. A scouted Fugitive stays on the map for 60 minutes, then “Target disappeared”. A button on your main city jumps to your next Fugitive. RULE DETAIL Fugitive Warrants 5 at event start. Unused ones are wiped at event end. Leading a rally Your own Fugitive: 15 Energy to scout and 20 to rally. No Warrant. Requesting assistance Costs 1 Warrant and turns your Fugitive into a target your allies rally. You must be in an alliance. Requests expire on a countdown. Refill The first 5 times you help an ally launch a Rally, you get a Warrant back. Daily caps 10 Rallies you lead and 50 you join, per day. Zero Warrants The button shows 0/1 and does nothing, with no error. Stages 1 to 5 Requesting assistance there gives your helpers extra Warrants. If you can clear your difficulty, spend spare Warrants here. Unconfirmed: that leading a rally on your own Fugitive needs no Warrant.

A solo stage costs 15 to scout and 10 to attack; a rallied stage 15 to scout and 20 to rally. Delicious Meals give 120 Energy at 00:00 and 12:00 UTC, six over the event. A detective investigates at the Detective Division. 3. A patrol car arrests, spawning 1 or more suspects. 4. Interrogation Room: +200 Satisfaction per suspect. 5. Then more and upgraded Police Cells and Interrogation Rooms, Chief Speech and Quick Response. Public Safety 0 to 100, hard-capped. Bands: Severe Risk (0), Elevated Risk (10), General Risk (50), Safe (100). It gates orders; Satisfaction is what you spend. Maritime Enforcement 5 days + 1 claim day Chief’s Office level 7+ 8-hour missions pre-release figures RULE DETAIL Window Five days, then a one-day claim period: you can claim, open and merge, but not deploy. Entry Chief’s Office level 7 or higher. Who scores You alone. Squads reset every event; an unlock lasts only the current run and cannot be bought after day five. Pays Storage Crate contents, merge results and Enforcement Count milestones. The headline reward is Legendary Universal Hero Fragments.

DO Redeploy every 8 hours. A squad does at most 3 missions a day, and every idle hour lowers that. Unlock Squad 2 (2,000 Diamonds): its 15 crates return about 3,450. Unlock Squad 3 (10,000) only if you want the fragments. Claim the free speedup daily. Tap the + next to your speedup count. Spend speedups just under a whole hour. At 7 hours 1 minute a mission costs 8; two minutes later, 7. Speed up one squad at a time when short, instead of Quick Speedup. Send every squad out just before day five ends. They finish on the claim day, and their crates can still be claimed. DON’T Open Lvl 2 crates on reflex. Three Lvl 2s are the only path to Lvl 3 and Lvl 4. Merge Lvl 1s that go nowhere. Merge only when the result completes a set of three Lvl 2s. Leave the tab during Auto-Enforcement. It stops.

RULE DETAIL What one does Removes exactly 1 hour from a mission, cost rounded up. It is the only way to shorten a mission. Universal Speedups and Diamonds do not work. RULE DETAIL Velvet Don target Alliance HQ, not your police station. The Suburb HQ first; the Countryside HQ only if no Suburb HQ is placed. Mobster rule Waves 7, 14 and 17 only attack chiefs who are online when they spawn. An offline chief never gets the wave. Two-defeat cap Two Defensive Defeats on your own police station and the Mafia stops attacking you for the rest of the run. You lose every remaining personal wave, and the biggest come late, wave 17 above all. You can still reinforce allies and defend HQ. HQ losses Losing the Alliance HQ battle does not count toward your personal cap. Squad waves Your squads at home defend your police station on their own. Mafia Squad waves can run on autopilot.

DO Be online for five alarms: +8:00, +14:30, +21:00, +26:30 and +33:00 from the start. Garrison HQ early with strong squads before +14:30 and +33:00. Decide in advance who garrisons. Reinforce constantly, above all into boss waves. Use the in-game request assistance ping. Defend every wave you are attacked on. Drive participation. The coin tiers and the Difficulty 2 unlock depend on the alliance total. DON’T Skip a Mobster. There is no make-up wave. Lose your own station twice. Two Defensive Defeats and the Mafia stops coming. Reinforce eliminated chiefs. A chief with two losses is no longer attacked, so it does nothing. Leave early. Leaving before payout wipes your alliance contribution and the alliance reward.

Two pools. Solo Defense Points are your own total: they feed the milestone tiers and the Solo leaderboard. Alliance Defense Points are every member’s total added up: they feed the difficulty unlocks and the Alliance leaderboard. RULE DETAIL Your own police station Every wave except 10 and 20. You bank the full wave score, flat, win or lose, even at zero kills. The 50% rule Eliminating 50% or more of a squad marks a “Defensive Victory”. That only sets the win or loss flag and a strike toward the two-defeat cap. It never touches your points. Waves 10 and 20 They hit Alliance HQ and are shared. Each defender inside banks only a kill-based portion of the wave, the same half-credit math as reinforcing. HQ space is limited, so not everyone gets in. Reinforcing an ally The defender still banks the full wave score; you earn points for the enemies you kill, at half credit. Realistic floor Your own-station waves total 299,400 at Difficulty 1 and about 314,000 at Difficulty 2 (the 18 waves that do not go to HQ). Exact half-credit formula, HQ kill share and HQ garrison space unknown.

Nobody at HQ when the Velvet Dons land (waves 10 and 20): about 57% of the event’s points. Treating the squad waves as the event. All 15 together are under 30% of the points. Not reinforcing. It adds points and costs the chief you help nothing. Thinking a Defensive Defeat scores nothing. You bank the full wave score at zero kills; a defeat costs a strike, not points.

Vault Trap 30-minute window 5:00 gather timer damage-based rewards online 10 minutes early RULE DETAIL Window 30 minutes. The vault closes at exactly 30:00. Gather timer Always 5:00, never 10:00. The last rally must start by about 5 minutes 20 seconds before the end. Who scores You alone, by personal damage total. Rank changes nothing. Pays Alliance Coins, materials, Ammo, Cash, Electricity and Gas in 20 brackets, plus separate achievements. Lockout Joining locks you out of both traps until 00:00 server time on the third calendar day. Two traps An alliance can own two but run one at a time. Each has a 47-hour cooldown after it closes.

DO Captains start on their turn, one stagger after the captain before them, gather timer 5:00. Join the next rally at the top of the list, and keep joining until the end. Send your strongest squads first with Vixen and Andre. Donate Tranquilizers before the run, up to 1,200. Tell leadership at once if you cannot stay the full 30 minutes. DON’T Cherry-pick rallies or wait for a better captain. Start your own rally when one is full; another starts within seconds. Start out of turn, early or late. Join a rogue rally. Officers cannot disband it; leadership calls it out in chat and the starter cancels. Mid-run, the rotation changes only by adding captains at the end or replacing one who left.

−10:00 Everyone online. Anyone who cannot stay the full 30 minutes says so. −5:00 Captain rotation posted in alliance chat. 0:00 The vault opens; the first captain starts at once. 6:30 left Last call: anyone, even with 1 hero or 1 troop, starts a rally. 5:20 left Hard deadline. A rally started later will not arrive. 0:00 left The vault closes at exactly 30:00. Joining with three squads at a 30-second stagger (time left in the run): TIME LEFT WHAT HAPPENS 30:00, 29:30, 29:00 You join rallies #1, #2 and #3 28:30 Rally #4 starts; you cannot join yet 25:00 Rally #1 launches 24:40 It arrives 24:20 It returns 23:30 Rally #4 launches Do not assume your next rally goes out the moment your first returns.

One rally cycle is 340 seconds: 5:00 to gather, 20 seconds to march to the vault, 20 seconds back. Divide by the number of captains and round up to the next 5 seconds. Each captain starts again one full cycle after their own last start. Stagger between captains Captains on the roster Stagger: 0 seconds 10 captains: 35-second stagger, about 43 rallies. 15 captains: 25 seconds, about 60. A member who joins a quarter of the rallies gets about 4 more joins from those 17 extra: about 2 million more damage at 500,000 a rally.

Joiners: Andre or Vixen lead your first two joins, your strongest squads. Their first-deployment skill gives the same penetration buff; put the higher skill level on the earlier rally. #1 Andre or Vixen, Scarlett, Lucy. #2 Andre or Vixen, your second-best Guard, your second-best Marksman. Without Andre, only #1: Vixen, Scarlett, Lucy. Your third join can be any squad: only its first hero’s first skill counts. Captains: lead with Brooke, Scarlett and Lucy. That leaves Andre free to lead your #2 join and Vixen your #3. A captain’s own joins with Andre: #2 Andre or Vixen, Gary, Tony; #3 Andre or Vixen, Leon, Rix. Without Andre: #2 Vixen, Leon, Tony. Without Brooke: #1 any lineup without Vixen, #2 Vixen, any Guard, any Biker. Leon, Cassie and Gus have no vault skills. Gen 2 and Gen 3 heroes not covered. Unconfirmed: whether Brooke or Andre should lead captain rallies. Skills that count: Brooke’s Fighting Spirit and Destructive Force, Scarlett’s Surprise Attack and Cold Killer, Lucy’s Ray of Sunshine, Andre’s War Cry, Vixen’s Armed to the Teeth. Skills that do nothing here: Unyielding Essence, Shadow Step and Sunny Sense. The vault never hits back, so damage-reduction skills are wasted. Troops: 10% Guards, 20% Bikers, 70% Marksmen (1:2:7) in every squad; always fill Marksmen up to 70%. A squad holds about 50,000 to 120,000 troops, so three take about 150,000 to 360,000.

RULE DETAIL Your bracket The highest damage threshold you reach in the run sets your bracket. Leader’s buffs Damage is boosted by the rally leader’s buffs, not your own. Joiner skills Among all joiners, only the first skill of each member’s first hero applies, and only the 4 highest-level of those take effect. Hero Exclusive Equipment skills do not count. Ties go to whoever joined first. The vault boss 0 attack, 0 penetration, a defense rating of 1, HP too large to empty, and no return damage. Skills that cut damage taken do nothing. Rank does nothing The final rankings message shows damage rank, but rewards follow your personal total. Energy Rallies cost no Chief Energy. To see your damage per run: tap the Vault on the state map, then Rewards, then Damage Rankings, then the small clipboard icon next to your name.

Members donate Tranquilizers before the run to raise the whole alliance’s damage against the Master of Heists. They come from daily intel missions, and each one donated earns 200 Alliance Coins. RULE DETAIL Achievements A separate 39-tier ladder keyed on your best personal damage in a single run, ever. Not mailed: claim each tier by hand. Tiers 1 to 5 10,000 to 500,000 damage. Starting a 10:00 gather timer, which breaks the timing for every captain behind you. Starting a rally with less than about 5 minutes 20 seconds left: it will not arrive. Leaving the alliance before the reward mail. Using a player-versus-player lineup built on damage-reduction skills.

Alliance Mobilization 6 days every 2 weeks alliance vs alliance Chief’s Office level 10+ RULE DETAIL Window 6 days on a two-week cycle, with a preview day before and a settlement day after. Entry 15 alliance members, counted before the event starts; your own Chief’s Office at level 10; at least one member logged in during the week before the start. No switching Changing alliance from the preview day onward ends your part in it. Leave and you are locked out at once, and any accepted task is cancelled. Rejoin the same alliance and access returns, unless it disbands. Who scores You (Solo Points) and your alliance (Alliance Points). The alliance total gates every milestone. Pays Milestone rewards, Solo and Alliance rank rewards, and Unlimited Mobilization Supplies (Alliance Coins and a chest). Daily reset Attempts and their prices reset every day and do not carry over.

DO Spend all nine attempts every day. Reroll first. Refresh Exclusive tiles free every 2 minutes until a 200% badge sits on a task you can clear from inventory. Take the smallest tier you can clear. When you hold more stock than you have attempts left today, take the bigger tier. Fill cheap attempts first: attempts 2 to 4 at 50 Diamonds before the top price. Push the alliance total. A Solo milestone pays nothing until the alliance reaches its threshold. Claim everything before the event ends. Clear dead Public tiles (R4 and above) so low-level members can use the board. DON’T Give up tasks. The attempt is burned. Accept an unbadged tile when a free reroll could double it. Save attempts for a final-day sprint. They are deleted at reset. Buy points with a Diamond task. Buy the 500-Diamond refresh except in the closing minutes. Finish a Legendary alliance at 10,000 points or less. It is demoted whatever its rank. Leave the alliance mid-event. Rejoining fixes it unless the alliance disbands.

You start each day with 9 attempts and can buy up to 10 more. You hold one task at a time. Accepted tasks expire on their own clock of 24, 36 or 48 hours, and must be finished before the event ends. RULE DETAIL Public board Shared, no badge, base score. Only R4 and above can refresh a tile nobody has accepted; the replacement takes 30 minutes and nobody can pay to skip it. Exclusive board Your own. Every tile carries a 120% or 200% badge, a straight multiplier on the score. Anyone can refresh for free; the replacement arrives in 2 minutes, with no daily limit. Level check Your Chief’s Office level is checked when you accept, not when you finish. A tile you are too low for cannot be taken and sits on the board until refreshed. Buying attempts Attempts 2 to 4 cost 50 Diamonds; the top price is 1,000 Diamonds. 500-Diamond refresh Only skips the 2-minute wait. It grants no attempt, task or point. Exclusive Tasks (C) ticket Lets you pick the task on an Exclusive tile: tap Select, pick, confirm. One ticket per pick; you need an attempt left and no task in hand. Give up a picked task and the ticket comes back; a picked task still open at the end expires and the ticket returns by mail. The list puts the biggest task first, so scroll to the smallest you can clear. Unknown: the attempt prices between 50 and 1,000 Diamonds, whether a ticket pick also spends an attempt, and the ticket pack’s contents and price.

The level in brackets is the Chief’s Office level a task needs; speedup tiers are in minutes. Each tier reads amount → points. Base scores at 100%. A 200% badge doubles them; a 120% badge multiplies by 1.2. Bros in Arms 48 hours solo leaderboard player vs player only Chief’s Office level 7+ RULE DETAIL Window 48 hours. The event page and calendar entry appear a day before it opens and vanish the moment it ends; there is no grace period to claim. Entry Chief’s Office level 7. Below that the event does not appear at all. Who scores You alone: no alliance board, no team score. Pays Four progress tiers (resources, Hero EXP, speedups, diamonds and Legendary skill books), then server rank rewards down to 1,000th place. Two versions Your server runs one of them. The first-place preview on the event page tells you which: diamonds and speedups is the old one, a Component and a Legendary Recruitment is the new one. DO Scout first, every time, in the same window as the attack. The Officer mix sets your payout, and scouting drops your shield anyway. Go wide, not tall. A spread of low-level Officers pays more per Power than a whale’s stack of the same size. Punch down freely. The level gate only blocks attacks on PDs 10 or more effective levels above you; nothing blocks the reverse and there is no scoring penalty, unlike State Showdown’s 3-level rule. Read the deeper report. Tap the enemy’s row in the battle report for the per-level table of kills, losses and injured. It is the only screen that shows what you scored. Batch your raids. Every attack opens a 30-minute window with no shield; six sessions is six exposures. DON’T Overreach. Too big a gap and you get a “Crushing Defeat” mail with no casualty table: you lose Officers and never see what happened. Hunt shielded PDs. Attack, Scout and Rally are all hard-blocked. Farm criminals. They are not Officers; the grind scores zero. Scouting, attacking or starting a rally drops your Tactical Shield and locks a new one for 30 minutes, longer while any of your marches is still in a fight.

RULE DETAIL Injuries still count for the attacker Your Hospital decides only whether your Officers come back. Still worth it: healing costs 10% of training. A T10 Guard costs 2,788 Ammo and 2,091 Cash to train, 279 and 209 to heal. Hospital overflow Past Hospital capacity your wounded go to the Recovery Center (see Marches › Garrison). Upgrade both before the event. Tactical Shield Blocks every attack and scout outright. Sizes: 2, 8, 24 and 72 hours. A 72-hour shield covers the whole event plus the preview day. Four things stop you shielding You attacked in the last 30 minutes; one of your marches is in a fight; your troops are in the Capitol, a Cannon, a Prison or an alliance facility; your police station is in a Forbidden Zone (teleporting into one also destroys a shield you have). Full rules: Defending your city. Moving away Random, Advanced, Alliance and Territory Teleporters all work during the event, and inbound attacks do not stop you. Only leading a rally, or an Alliance Teleporter with squads deployed, blocks it. Governor help Ask your Governor for Forced Teleportation (see Capital War). Two defenses that do not exist The Security Wall does not stop attacks, and there is no attack cooldown: you can be farmed back to back for as long as you stay unshielded.

Joint Escort no Officer losses cross-server PvP about 2 days active Chief’s Office level 12+ RULE DETAIL Window Preview 1 day before. Escort runs about 2 days in 24-hour sub-phases that reset at UTC midnight. Results is a 20-hour wrap-up with no new dispatches or raids. Entry Chief’s Office level 7 shows the event. Level 12 lets you dispatch, raid or request an Assist Squad. Who scores Each player on their own trucks and raids. There is no leaderboard. Pays A fixed Safe resource bundle per truck plus random items. Raids seize part of other trucks’ cargo; helping an ally’s truck arrive pays a Support Reward. Caps per sub-phase 4 dispatches, 4 raids, 2 trucks on the road at once, 1 Assist invite. Last day The final sub-phase is 28 hours: dispatch closes after the first 24, and the last 4 hours are raid-only.

DO Refresh before you dispatch. Each refresh has better odds, and the sixth is a guaranteed SSR. Use Escort Permits first. Save the Assist invite for an SSR. You get one per sub-phase. Raid SSR trucks first. One SSR raid pays 250,000 each of Ammo and Cash, the same as a whole N truck. Start big upgrades after you dispatch. Officer upgrades reach trucks already on the road. Plan the last dispatch. A 4-hour truck sent on the last day arrives right at event close. Move on after a failed raid. The 10-minute cooldown covers only the same target. DON’T Expect a swap. Heroes are locked once dispatched. Reuse heroes across trucks. Two trucks at once need 6 different heroes. Raid a burned-out truck. After 2 raids it is safe for the rest of its trip; heavy smoke and fire mark it. Look for alliance targets. Your own, alliance members’ and arrived trucks cannot be raided.

RULE DETAIL Dispatch Pick heroes, refresh quality if you want, send. One dispatch sends one truck. Travel 3 to 4 hours, set by the server and shown on the truck panel before you confirm. A random route with 5 waypoints. On the road 2 trucks at most at once. When one arrives you can send another. Heroes Up to 3 per truck, one per type (Guard, Biker, Marksman), locked once dispatched. Officers Supplied from HQ at the highest level you can train. Level, count and stat changes reach a truck already on the road. Fight An Arena-style fight: the raider’s 3 heroes and Officers against the escort heroes, any Assist heroes and their Officers. You get a normal PvP report. Cross-server Trucks from other servers show on your map with a server tag (for example #7). “Hide same-server trucks” filters your own server. Arrival You collect what is left on board. The 20-hour Results phase settles late arrivals.

RULE DETAIL Publishing a squad Post up to 3 heroes for your alliance. They stay free for your own trucks. Inviting a squad One alliance Assist Squad per truck, 1 invite per sub-phase. Its heroes join your truck’s defense for that trip. Lock A squad supports one truck at a time and stays locked until that truck arrives. Support Reward When an ally invites your squad and their truck arrives: 5 level 2 Resource Chest (C) and 5 five-minute Universal Speedups, by mail. Limit 3 Support Rewards a day.

Oilfield Strike 30 minutes free-for-all free Officers 5-tier tech tree RULE DETAIL Window 30 minutes exactly. Oil still being mined or marching home counts at 30:00. Settlement mail at 30:10. Entry All squad queues must be empty: you cannot enter with active marches. Who scores You alone, against everyone in your arena. Players can attack your occupied oilfields, alliance members included. Pays Collection milestones, final rank rewards (Diamonds are the headline) and the Refinery rank, which pays oil. Key times 9:00 warning, 10:00 hidden fields (phase 1), 19:00 warning, 20:00 hidden fields (phase 2), 23:00 Refinery for 7 minutes.

DO 0:00: teleport into Zone 3 next to at least 3 close Lv. 3 oilfields. Send all squads but one to Lv. 3 fields; the last one hunts Armed Patrols for tech. Run the probe squad on scattered oil the whole battle. 9:00 and 19:00: recall from regular fields so your squads can race the hidden fields at 10:00 and 20:00. 23:00: send one squad to the Refinery, whatever your power. If a few seconds there make rank 10, that is 20,000 oil, more than 10 minutes on a Lv. 3 (19,200). Phase 2 hidden fields end at 25:00, so recall to the Refinery at 23:00. Use all 5 free teleports (0:00, 6:00, 12:00, 18:00, 24:00): after draining a cluster, move to a fresh one worth 30,000+ oil. Take Trickle at tech tier 1. DON’T Enter with active marches. All squad queues must be empty. Fight what you cannot beat. Recall instead: recalling keeps your oil. Keep attacking with 2+ heroes in recovery. Collect and probe instead.

Always send one squad at 23:00: rank 10 pays 20,000 oil for a few seconds, 2,000 to 4,000 oil a second against 32 on a Lv. 3. Open for 7 minutes; ranked by total seconds held, and 1 second qualifies. One or two big players fight over ranks 1 to 3. One squad per player at the Refinery or on the way. Its oil counts toward your collection total.

Your score is the total oil collected across the whole battle. Every normal oilfield drains in exactly 18 minutes at base speed, so a Lv. 3 means fewer captures, not a faster drain. Chase one when idle and within 30 seconds of march: 30 seconds out, 20 to drain and 30 back is 4,000 oil in 80 seconds, about 3,000 oil a minute. When to stay put. Stay on your Lv. 3 if the hidden field is 60+ grid squares away, or the refresh tooltip shows it is already 50%+ drained. Scattered oil drops are 1,000 to 6,000 oil each, collected by a free probe squad that takes no queue slot. Guards pay no tech experience. Only Armed Patrols do.

Police Department Assessment 6 themes, weekly 1,800 total stages 5 failures per theme per day Chief’s Office level 19 RULE DETAIL Window A weekly rotation on UTC, not local time. If a theme closes while you are in it, the game kicks you out and closes every PD Assessment window. Entry Three gates, all required: Chief’s Office level 19, a built Command Center, and a state open at least 4 weeks. Enter through the Command Center’s PD Assessment ring entry or the sidebar shortcut. Who scores You alone. Pays Assessment Coins (20 on first clear, 10 per sweep), briefcases, fibers, chests and 14 milestones. Cadence Failures reset at 00:00 UTC. Weekly stage progress resets when a theme closes; Highest Stage never resets. Cost One of your five daily failures, and only if you lose.

DO Sweep before you push. Sweep only works while you are below your best stage. Park on multiples of 10. Every 10th stage pays a Premium Assessment Briefcase on each sweep; Auto-Advance already stops there. Clear easy stages first. Wins are free; probe walls last. Deepen your strongest system. The ladder gets cheaper the deeper you are. Fill your capacity. The game warns if you deploy under cap. Spend Coins in the buy order on Shops › Police Department Assessment store. DON’T Park on odd stages. Stopping at 51 or 63 wastes the sweep drops. Burn consumables. They do nothing in any theme. Test walls on Sunday. Only 5 failures for the week. Pour into K9 for score. It caps at 150 stages. Buy speedups. 16,000 Coins for 40 hours, 35.4% of the shop. Trust the power number. A client-side estimate that leaves VIP out and never decides the result.

RULE DETAIL Failures Tracked per theme and reset at 00:00 UTC. No buyback with Diamonds, items or resets. Sweep Unlocks at Highest Stage 10. Re-clears the whole range instantly. Auto-Advance Unlocks at Highest Stage 30 (shown in-game as Stage 3-10). A win queues the next stage after 5 seconds. It stops at every 10th stage; switch it back on. Quick Challenge Offered when your power far exceeds the requirement; jumps you forward. Capacity in K9, Badge and Equipment Locked at 150,000, the same as the enemy, every stage. A pure stat contest. Troops in the five single-system themes 250,000 each of Royal Guard, Royal Biker and Royal Marksman, level 10, free. Troops in Comprehensive Your own troops at real strength. Under 600,000 troops of level 6 or higher, you are topped up with 250,000 of each level-6 type, spent first. Tech Raises stats and capacity: it double-dips. Hero Selection capacity Starts at 150,000, plus each deployed hero’s troop number, plus hero-sourced bonus. Teams Three heroes per team: one Guard, one Biker, one Marksman. No hero in two teams. Squad walls In Hero Selection and Comprehensive the enemy fields identical squads: 1 for stages 1-50, 2 for 51-250, 3 for 251-350. Fights are sequential. Hero Selection’s total enemy power runs 12.0M to 33.4M, then 66.1M to 208.3M with 6 heroes needed, then 311.0M to 398.9M with 9.

Each theme gets 5 failures per day it runs: 10 a week for every two-day theme. Sunday’s Comprehensive Assessment gets 5 for the week. Joint Confiscation Point 24 hours Alliance level 8+ 50 members or more R4/R5 place RULE DETAIL Window 24 hours from placement. A squad gathers until it is full or the point expires. Entry Alliance level 8 or higher, 50 or more members, and Reclaim Territory has ended (pass or fail). R4 or R5 places it. Who gathers Every member of the placing alliance, one squad each. No one else can. Pays Safe Ammo, Cash, Electricity or Gas, depending on the point type. Cost 200,000 each of Alliance Ammo, Cash, Electricity and Gas: 800,000 in total, the same for all four types. Versus a normal Lvl 8 tile Same gather rate; squads cannot be attacked or scouted; pays Safe resources.

DO Gather here first. Before any normal tile while a point is up. At base speed one member can take about 10.3 million Ammo or Cash (or 2.05 million Electricity, or 513,000 Gas) in 24 hours, before walk time. Place it central. Near the middle of members’ cities, not the edge of the territory. Every minute a squad walks is a minute it does not gather. Announce it in chat. Members get a mail, but the push toggle is hidden, so most miss it. Pick the type by need. Choose what members are short on; all four fill a squad in the same time. Send a full squad straight back out. Check the time left first: a squad sent near the end gathers only until expiry. DON’T Re-place to switch type. All types share one slot and the demolish screen shows no refund. Sit at 49 members. Under 50 members the points stay locked. Send a second squad. The game allows one squad per member.

Each type fills a squad in the same time: 2 hours 20 minutes at base speed. Speeds are before buffs; squad loads are an example squad with no buffs.

You collect speed × hours on the point. A bigger squad just means fewer trips. The point panel shows your Confiscation Speed with buffs included. RULE DETAIL Unlock Alliance Lvl 8 or higher, 50 or more members, Reclaim Territory ended (a failed milestone counts), R4 or R5 to place. Find the blocker The Tip button on the Special Buildings tab shows Alliance Level x/8, Members x/50 and the milestone status. How Alliance Territory, Special Buildings tab, Joint Confiscation Points. Push Place on the type, drag the footprint to a valid spot, confirm. Members get a mail. Where Inside your own finished alliance territory, on your own State, on an empty tile with the fog cleared. Not on terrain obstacles or battleground areas. Suburb and Downtown Suburb tiles need the Suburban Development alliance tech; Downtown tiles need Downtown Development. Cooldown None between placements. The only limits are the one slot and alliance stock. Refund The demolish screen shows zero.

RULE DETAIL One squad each A second squad is refused. Heroes in the squad count toward confiscation buffs. Safe on the point No other alliance gets a Confiscate, attack or scout button on a squad there. Marching Speedups Marching Speedup I (25%) and II (50%) speed the trips out and back, not the gathering. Use them only near the end of a point’s life. Yield levers Resource Confiscation Speed buffs first; then type buffs such as Gas Confiscation I and II, Honor buildings, a high-capacity squad and a central point.

K9 dogs state day 55 5 dogs always active no hero battles RULE DETAIL Window Permanent, not a timed event. Radar and Magnus arrive from state day 72. Entry K9 Tactical Center, state day 55. Each dog needs the one before it at a set level. Who scores You alone. Contraband Crates can be shared with allies. Pays Account-wide troop buffs, daily utility skills and Special Operations rewards. Daily limits 2 Frisbee sessions and 2 Agility runs per dog, a daily deploy budget and 5 ally-crate claims. All reset daily. Ties to other systems Special Operations spend Energy and Beacon’s skill restores it. Magnus’s debuff works in squad battles; Alliance Training has a K9 button.

DO Race the chain. Level each new dog to 15 at once: that opens the next dog, and every owned dog’s buffs count all the time. Reach Rank 1 early. Lvl 10 plus the first Breakthrough unlocks the Skill and the next level cap. Favor Radar and Magnus. Their buffs end three times Foreman’s. Level to the Drill breakpoint, then drill. Use Auto-Drill after 20 manual Drills. Keep all 3 mission slots working. Missions always pay. Fire Beacon’s Energy skill, then deploy. Use every daily cap. 2 Frisbee sessions and 2 Agility runs per dog, the deploy budget and 5 ally-crate claims reset daily. DON’T Look for an equip button. There isn’t one. Expect hero-battle help. Dogs add nothing there. Tap the city dog for loot. It is a one-time unlock. Replace a worse roll. Retry instead, or let Auto-Drill handle it.

Level each new dog to 15 straight away: that opens the next one. DOG OPENS NEEDS Foreman State day 55 Nothing: first dog Beacon State day 55 Foreman at Lvl 1+ Buggy State day 55 Beacon at Lvl 15+ Radar State day 72 Buggy at Lvl 15+, then Agility Training Magnus State day 72 Radar at Lvl 15+, then Agility Training Frisbee Training: 5 throws a session. Perfect adds 30%, Outstanding 15%, a Mistake nothing. Progress carries over and the tame completes at 100%, so four Perfect throws finish it in one session. 2 sessions per dog per day. Agility Training (Radar and Magnus): a three-lane runner. 30 coins wins and 3 hits end the run. Each coin adds 2%, kept when a run fails; a won run is worth 60%, so two won runs finish a tame. 2 runs per dog per day, separate from Frisbee. Dog stats have no effect.

Level and Breakthrough raise Squad Attack and Squad Defense by a percentage. The range runs from the first level to the maximum. DOG QUALITY MAX SQUAD ATK/DEF Foreman 1 Lvl 50, Rank 5 +0.05% → +2.50% Beacon 2 Lvl 60, Rank 6 +0.08% → +5.03% Buggy 2 Lvl 60, Rank 6 +0.08% → +5.03% Radar 3 Lvl 70, Rank 7 +0.11% → +7.54% Magnus 3 Lvl 70, Rank 7 +0.11% → +7.54% Beacon and Buggy end at twice Foreman’s buff; Radar and Magnus at three times. Drills add the rest: six attributes, Health and Penetration for Marksman, Biker and Guard, by percentage.

RULE DETAIL Leveling vs Breakthrough Alternate them. Leveling spends K9 Kibble. Breakthrough spends rarer materials, adds a bigger Squad step and power, upgrades the Skill and raises the level cap. At the cap the button says “Breakthrough” instead of “Level Up”. Level cap by rank Foreman: Rank 0 Lvl 10, Rank 1 Lvl 20, Rank 2 Lvl 30, Rank 3 Lvl 40, Rank 4 and 5 Lvl 50. The last Breakthrough adds power and a Skill rank but no levels. Beacon and Buggy go one tier higher (Rank 6, Lvl 60), Radar and Magnus two (Rank 7, Lvl 70); their per-rank caps are missing. Drilling Each Drill rerolls all six attributes for one Whistle. No per-stat lock. Replace commits the new values (it warns if the total drops); Retry throws the pending roll away. Quality ratchet Each attribute starts Common. Reaching the cap for its tier promotes it: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary. It never drops back. Premium Whistles lean toward better rolls. Drill tier by level Common Lvl 10, Uncommon Lvl 20, Rare Lvl 30, Epic Lvl 40, Legendary Lvl 50. Auto-Drill Unlocks after 20 manual Drills. Set a Whistle budget. It keeps rolls where the six attributes add up higher and stops when Whistles run out or all six are maxed for your level. It drops a final net-negative roll and leaves a net-zero roll pending. The check is on the total, so one attribute can fall.

Sapphire Bay is your own island: a 60 by 60 grid that starts under fog and coconut trees. You clear it and place decorations, and the decorations and the Tiki Bar give permanent buffs to your whole account, not just on the island. The island store needs Chief’s Office level 19.

RESOURCE WHAT IT IS FOR WHERE IT COMES FROM Coconut Cocktails the island’s money: Tiki Bar and Workshop upgrades, the Sapphire Bay Store the Tiki Bar, chopped trees (720 wood = 1 cocktail), supply crates, tasks, the sign-in, helping allies, later the Processing Plant Prosperity the island’s score: Tiki Bar upgrades need it, the rankings use it placed decorations only

1 Workshop workers chop trees by themselves; the wood turns into cocktails (720 wood = 1 cocktail). 2 The Tiki Bar makes cocktails on its own: 120 an hour at level 1, 300 at level 7. It holds 12 hours; claim before it fills or the rest is lost. 3 Spend cocktails on the Tiki Bar (more buffs, more cocktails) and on Workshops (faster clearing). 4 Buy decorations in the Sapphire Bay Store and place them: every one adds Prosperity, and Rare and Epic ones add a buff. 5 When every tree is gone, the Coconut Processing Plant opens: 40 cocktails an hour per worker.
Two rules that save the most time

1 Keep the Island screen open. Workers chop at full speed only while you are on the Island screen; anywhere else, even elsewhere in the game, they work at half speed. 2 Tiki Bar level 3 first. It puts you on the rankings and lets allies help you, and from then on three helps a day are free cocktails for both sides.
Where to put your effort, in order

1 Tiki Bar level 3. Place the cheap Common decorations and the Day 1 sign-in decoration for the Prosperity it needs. 2 Help three allies a day and open the map. A second Workshop comes at Tiki Bar level 5; take every Workshop to level 4 (two workers) before pushing one higher, and clear toward the crates. 3 One of each Rare and Epic decoration, then upgrade. Combat accounts: the six Epic class decorations. Economy accounts: the four Rare confiscation decorations (+30% each). Builders: Open-air Cinema, Large Bonfire, Seaside Hot Spring. 4 Clear every tree. That opens the Processing Plant and the last crates, and lets you remove the Workshops. 5 The long grind. The top Tiki Bar levels, decorations to level 5, and the Lighthouse; keep every Universal Decoration Construction Blueprint for it.

Before you can land you sail a 3-day voyage in real time: a log entry every 3 hours, each with a small reward. It cannot be sped up, so claim the entries as they come. DAY WHERE REWARD 1 White Wave Island 5 resource items, 2 speedups, 2 components 2 Echo Island 5 resource items, 3 speedups, 3 components 3 Sapphire Bay the island opens

Opens only when every tree on the island is cleared (Workshops can then be removed). One level only: 40 cocktails an hour per worker, storage 2,000. At one worker it fills in about 50 hours, so claim it every day.

The island is a 60 by 60 grid. (0, 0) is the bottom corner, where you start; higher numbers are deeper in. Coconut Workshop workers chop by themselves, always the frontier tree (one touching cleared ground) nearest their Workshop, so the clearing spreads in a rough half-circle around each Workshop rather than a straight line. You steer it only by where you put Workshops. Functional decorations add Prosperity; Rare and Epic ones also give a permanent buff. Cosmetic ones (paths, fences, plants, water, bought with diamonds or cash) give neither. Max active: only that many copies of one decoration count; extra copies do nothing. Common 2–4, Uncommon 2–5, Rare and Epic 1, so collect one of each and upgrade it. Upgrading uses spare level 1 copies of the same decoration from the Island Warehouse: 2, 3, 4 and 5 copies for levels 2 to 5, so 15 copies in all for one decoration at level 5. Dismantling (anything but the Tiki Bar and Workshops) gives every level 1 copy back. The Recycle Shop turns spare decorations into cocktails. Never recycle Universal Decoration Construction Blueprints: 10 make a Lighthouse Blueprint.
